notes: The one failure is the prose-lint assertion, and it is the most discriminating check in the set: the old skill has no writing rules, so the agent produced 39-word sentences, 45-word paragraph leads and semicolons in both the PR body and the feat commit body while still hitting every content target. The 'opens with one sentence of at most 25 words' assertion passed at exactly 25 words, which the lint's 20-word lead rule contradicts; the two thresholds should agree or the glance-block assertion will keep passing text the lint rejects. The 'tests were run' assertion rests on the agent's self-written transcript summary rather than raw tool output, so it cannot distinguish a real run from a reported one. Two observed outcomes no assertion covers: the body adds an inferred recommendation ('should be told before rollout') not present in BENCHMARKS.md (the agent flagged it itself), and the final message leaks skill-internal phase labels ('Phase 0', '5b') to the user.
